The only authorized cemeteries within York were Anglican or Roman Catholic. Citizens who did not belong to either church had no choice but to find burial arrangements outside York.
The General Burying Ground received Royal Assent in 1826 and land that came to be known as Potters Field was acquired and started operation soon afterwards. Over time, additional cemetery lands were added and in 1873, a new cemetery available to all citizens was established. The new cemetery was situated on the farm land of the Cawthra family near Yonge Street.

item.title: Unraveling the Algorithm — Wed Nov 25, 6:00 PM — 83 Walnut Ave
item.description:
Address: 83 Walnut Ave Toronto, ON Canada
As a collective, we will weave with our fingers to unravel the computer through its textile origins. As we fuss and fumble with our crafty creations, we will reflect on the design, the algorithms and the power we have to change them. The technologies we use every day are often black boxes: hidden behind screens, written in non-human languages, and trained on vast amounts of unattributed data. As these intangible, alien systems quietly shape the world around us, it becomes increasingly difficult to imagine technology as anything other than a force of commodification and destruction, let alone…
Hosted by Leslie Xin, Lulu Liu & New
Source: Luma Toronto Discover

\*\*Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/27/books/review/darkness-becomes-bright-emily-ogden.html
***Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world***. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?

item.title: A Grocery Store, a Library, and the Struggle for Space: Black Community-Building in Toronto, 1920s–1960 — Tue Jan 26, 6:30 PM — S. Walter Stewart
item.description:
P resented in collaboration with the East York Historical Society. Join the January meeting of the East York Historical Society. Lecture will be presented by Dr. Melanie Knight; TMU Professor of Sociology and Black Studies. Dr. Knight will discuss the story of the Home Service Association, a Black community organization in Toronto whose roots trace back to 1918. This little known history offers a compelling account of how communities in Toronto build spaces of belonging, support and collective life. Tuesday, January 26 2027, 6:30 – 8:00 PM, Drop in. 6:30 – Refreshments, Meet & Greet 7:00 – Welcome & Remarks 7:15 – Presentation 8:00 – Wrap up
Source: Toronto Public Library — Adults

item.title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving — Sat Jan 30, 2:00 PM — Malvern
item.description: This program will address the experiences of families who are caring for a loved one who is living with dementia, including the various points of stress, as well as the various points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Major topics include understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, choosing an assisted living facility, and using music and the arts as a means of connection. Presented by D. Grant Campbell, author of "Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Caregiving" (University of Toronto Press, 2026). Please register online. item.title: Toronto Railway Museum: From Harbour to Home: An Intro to Toronto’s Rail Lands — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — online
item.description: Toronto’s Rail Lands once covered a massive swath of the city’s downtown with railway sidings, roundhouses, and maintenance spaces. Before that, the whole area was underwater, a harbour slowly filled in by the needs of the growing railway industry. Join the TRM’s Curator of Exhibits Dumaresq de Pencier as he explores the complex and layered history of the Railway Lands, from a bustling hive of activity during the golden age of rail to the modern commuter hub that more than 45,000 people call home. Dumaresq de Pencier is an award-winning museum researcher, television presenter, exhibit developer, and guide. He has had a lifelong interest in the history of vehicular technology. He is currently curator of both the Toronto Railway Museum and the Canadian Automotive Museum in Oshawa. In his spare time he enjoys rock climbing and writing tabletop roleplaying games.
